## Module to write
path: StarterPlayerScripts/ShopUi.client.luau
purpose: Feature: Shop UI built with the UI kit (the house Theme, rounded panels, big readable buttons): a 'SHOP' button on the left edge of the HUD opens a panel listing every upgrade from ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades as cards (color swatch, name, effect text, cost, and state: Owned / Locked (needs X) / Buy). Pressing Buy sends a BuyUpgrade RemoteEvent; the server (UpgradeService) validates plot ownership, requires and cost exactly like a pad touch, then replies with the updated owned list so cards refresh. Cards the player cannot afford are dimmed; the panel closes with an X button or the same SHOP button. Must fit a phone-width screen. Bump counters shop_opened and shop_purchases. -- Client-only shop UI in its own ScreenGui (ResetOnSpawn=false). It builds a 'SHOP' button on the left edge of the screen, vertically centered and clear of the Cash HUD, that toggles a rounded panel with a title, an X close button and a ScrollingFrame list. The panel uses scale sizing with a UISizeConstraint (max about 420x520) so it fits a phone-width screen, and the text is large and readable. It requires ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades and iterates every upgrade, using that module's exact existing field names for id, name, cost, requires and effect. If there is no effect-text field, it builds the effect text from the data fields that exist. Each card shows a color swatch, name, effect text, cost, and a state button. Owned shows a disabled 'Owned' label. Locked shows 'Locked (needs <name of required upgrade>)' when a required id is not owned. Otherwise it shows a 'Buy' button. Cards where cost exceeds the Cash leaderstat are dimmed (transparency and darker text), and this refreshes on leaderstats Cash.Changed. It WaitForChilds the remotes ReplicatedStorage/BuyUpgrade and ReplicatedStorage/ShopSync with a timeout and fails soft if they are missing. Opening the panel does ShopSync:FireServer() to request the owned list. It listens to ShopSync.OnClientEvent(ownedIds) (an array of upgrade ids) and re-renders the cards. Pressing Buy calls BuyUpgrade:FireServer(upgradeId), with a short client cooldown, and the client never changes the owned state itself. The X button and the SHOP button both close the panel. It sends only intent and does no telemetry. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: shop_opened, shop_purchases.
depends: ReplicatedStorage/UiTheme.luau, ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades.luau

```luau
--!strict
-- UiTheme: pure shared UI kit for the house Theme (no side effects, no server code).
-- Palette matches the HUD / cash look: yellow Primary, green Good, red Bad, blue Info, dark Ink outlines.
-- Telemetry (shop_opened, shop_purchases) is counted by the server-side owner of those events, not here.

local UiTheme = {}

-- Colors
UiTheme.ink = Color3.fromRGB(28, 22, 38)
UiTheme.cream = Color3.fromRGB(255, 248, 232)
UiTheme.panel = Color3.fromRGB(255, 248, 232)
UiTheme.card = Color3.fromRGB(255, 255, 255)
UiTheme.text = Color3.fromRGB(28, 22, 38)
UiTheme.accent = Color3.fromRGB(255, 196, 41)
UiTheme.good = Color3.fromRGB(88, 214, 92)
UiTheme.bad = Color3.fromRGB(240, 68, 64)
UiTheme.info = Color3.fromRGB(64, 170, 255)
UiTheme.dim = Color3.fromRGB(190, 184, 176)
UiTheme.locked = Color3.fromRGB(120, 112, 134)

-- Fonts and metrics
UiTheme.font = Enum.Font.FredokaOne
UiTheme.headerFont = Enum.Font.LuckiestGuy
UiTheme.cornerRadius = 14
UiTheme.stroke = 3
UiTheme.minButtonHeight = 48 -- at least 44 px touch target
UiTheme.padding = 10

-- Adds a UICorner to a GuiObject (reuses an existing one).
function UiTheme.roundify(guiObject: GuiObject, radius: number?)
	local corner = guiObject:FindFirstChildOfClass("UICorner")
	if not corner then
		corner = Instance.new("UICorner")
		corner.Parent = guiObject
	end
	(corner :: UICorner).CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, radius or UiTheme.cornerRadius)
end

-- Returns a big readable TextButton.
-- props: text, size, position, anchorPoint, color, textColor, parent, name, zIndex, layoutOrder, onClick
function UiTheme.makeButton(props: { [string]: any }): TextButton
	local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
	button.Name = props.name or "Button"
	button.Text = props.text or ""
	local size: UDim2 = props.size or UDim2.fromOffset(160, UiTheme.minButtonHeight)
	if size.Y.Offset < UiTheme.minButtonHeight and size.Y.Scale == 0 then
		size = UDim2.new(size.X.Scale, size.X.Offset, 0, UiTheme.minButtonHeight)
	end
	button.Size = size
	button.Position = props.position or UDim2.fromOffset(0, 0)
	button.AnchorPoint = props.anchorPoint or Vector2.new(0, 0)
	button.BackgroundColor3 = props.color or UiTheme.accent
	button.TextColor3 = props.textColor or UiTheme.cream
	button.Font = UiTheme.headerFont
	button.TextScaled = true
	button.AutoButtonColor = true
	button.BorderSizePixel = 0
	button.ZIndex = props.zIndex or 1
	button.LayoutOrder = props.layoutOrder or 0

	UiTheme.roundify(button, UiTheme.cornerRadius)

	local border = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	border.Thickness = UiTheme.stroke
	border.Color = UiTheme.ink
	border.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border
	border.Parent = button

	local textStroke = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	textStroke.Thickness = UiTheme.stroke
	textStroke.Color = UiTheme.ink
	textStroke.ApplyStrokeMode = Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
	textStroke.Parent = button

	local pad = Instance.new("UIPadding")
	pad.PaddingTop = UDim.new(0.16, 0)
	pad.PaddingBottom = UDim.new(0.16, 0)
	pad.PaddingLeft = UDim.new(0, 6)
	pad.PaddingRight = UDim.new(0, 6)
	pad.Parent = button

	local minSize = Instance.new("UISizeConstraint")
	minSize.MinSize = Vector2.new(44, UiTheme.minButtonHeight)
	minSize.Parent = button

	local onClick = props.onClick
	if typeof(onClick) == "function" then
		button.Activated:Connect(function()
			onClick()
		end)
	end

	if props.parent then
		button.Parent = props.parent
	end
	return button
end

return UiTheme
```

### ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades.luau
```luau
-- Upgrades: pure data for the dropper / ore tier / speed / cash multiplier tree.
-- No requires, no side effects. Returns { list = {...}, byId = {...}, ores = {...} }.
--
-- BUDGET MATH (a full tree takes about 8-10 minutes)
--   Total cost of all 10 upgrades:
--     10 + 30 + 60 + 100 + 200 + 350 + 500 + 800 + 1500 + 2500 = 6050 cash
--   Base income is 1 dropper x 1 cash / 2 s = 0.5 cash/s. The first buy (10) is covered by a
--   small starter grant / early income so it lands within ~10 s of claiming a plot.
--   Income after each milestone (cubes per 2 s cycle x ore value x cash multiplier, per second):
--     dropper2                    2 x 1 x 1.0 / 2 =  1.0 /s
--     tier_silver                 2 x 3 x 1.0 / 2 =  3.0 /s
--     dropper3                    3 x 3 x 1.0 / 2 =  4.5 /s
--     mult1 (x1.5)                3 x 3 x 1.5 / 2 =  6.75/s
--     tier_gold                   3 x 8 x 1.5 / 2 = 18   /s
--     dropper4                    4 x 8 x 1.5 / 2 = 24   /s
--     mult2 (x2)                  4 x 8 x 2.0 / 2 = 32   /s
--     tier_diamond                4 x 20 x 2.0 / 2 = 80  /s
--   (speed upgrades only shorten the trip to the collector; they raise throughput of cubes
--   in flight, not value per cube.) Rough timeline: ~20 s to dropper2 + silver (40 cash),
--   ~60 s to speed1 + dropper3, ~2 min for mult1, ~3.5 min for gold, ~5 min for speed2 and
--   dropper4, ~7 min for mult2, and ~8-10 min for diamond (2500 at ~32/s plus pacing and
--   walking between pads). Players who skip around the tree finish slightly faster or slower,
--   but the tail cost (mult2 + diamond = 4000 of 6050) keeps the full tree near 8-10 minutes.
--
-- Effect shapes:
--   { kind = "dropper",  slots = n }   total active dropper slots after purchase
--   { kind = "tier",     tier = n }    ore tier every dropper spits out (index into ores)
--   { kind = "speed",    mult = x }    conveyor speed multiplier
--   { kind = "cashMult", mult = x }    collector cash multiplier

local list = {
	{ id = "dropper2", name = "Dropper 2", cost = 10, requires = nil, effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 2 } },
	{ id = "tier_silver", name = "Silver Ore", cost = 30, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 2 } },
	{ id = "speed1", name = "Speed 1", cost = 60, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "speed", mult = 1.5 } },
	{ id = "dropper3", name = "Dropper 3", cost = 100, requires = "dropper2", effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 3 } },
	{ id = "mult1", name = "Cash x1.5", cost = 200, requires = "tier_silver", effect = { kind = "cashMult", mult = 1.5 } },
	{ id = "tier_gold", name = "Gold Ore", cost = 350, requires = "tier_silver", effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 3 } },
	{ id = "speed2", name = "Speed 2", cost = 500, requires = "speed1", effect = { kind = "speed", mult = 2 } },
	{ id = "dropper4", name = "Dropper 4", cost = 800, requires = "dropper3", effect = { kind = "dropper", slots = 4 } },
	{ id = "mult2", name = "Cash x2", cost = 1500, requires = "mult1", effect = { kind = "cashMult", mult = 2 } },
	{ id = "tier_diamond", name = "Diamond Ore", cost = 2500, requires = "tier_gold", effect = { kind = "tier", tier = 4 } },
}

-- Indexed by tier.
local ores = {
	{ name = "Bronze", value = 1, color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 127, 50), material = Enum.Material.Metal, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Silver", value = 3, color = Color3.fromRGB(205, 210, 220), material = Enum.Material.Metal, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Gold", value = 8, color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 205, 40), material = Enum.Material.Foil, sparkles = false },
	{ name = "Diamond", value = 20, color = Color3.fromRGB(80, 235, 255), material = Enum.Material.Glass, sparkles = true },
}

local byId = {}
for _, upgrade in ipairs(list) do
	byId[upgrade.id] = upgrade
end

return {
	list = list,
	byId = byId,
	ores = ores,
}

```

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value.
- Touched fires many times per touch: debounce per player (a per-player cooldown or a one-time purchased flag) and check and deduct cost in the same step to prevent double-buys or double-spends.
- Define the data shape that a builder module returns (field names such as origin, gate, spawn) once, and have consumers use those exact fields. Do not add `a or b` fallbacks for guessed names.

## Fixing and debugging
- A "sync" StudioError about not being able to serve a path is an infrastructure or environment failure, not a code bug. Do not change game code in response. Retry the step.
- If the critic says a code path was never exercised in the playtest, fix the pacing or setup so the path actually runs (e.g. cheaper first purchase) instead of only adding more code.
- When the spec changes the flow (e.g. from auto-assign to claim), rewrite the entry script (Game.server) to require and wire the new modules, and delete the old flow's logic (slots, teleport on join). Updating only the new modules leaves the old behaviour running.
- After a redesign, check that every module is required by the entry script and that its init function is called. Unwired modules never run, and their counters never fire.

## UI kit (house style for all UI: paste the snippets you use, Theme first, and adapt; plain Luau, not modules)
- Chunky text: every label gets a dark UIStroke (2.5-4 px). LuckiestGuy for titles/numbers, FredokaOne for body. Never default or thin fonts.
- One palette everywhere: yellow Primary = main action, green Good = affordable/claim, red Bad = close/can't, blue Info = secondary, dark Ink outlines.
- Depth: UICorner 12-18 px, UIStroke border, light-top UIGradient fill, hard drop shadow 4-6 px below.
- Everything moves: appear with a Back-eased UIScale pop (0 -> 1), react with a punch (1.2 -> 1), press squish to 0.9. Tween UIScale, not Size; 0.1-0.4 s, never linear.
- Numbers tick up and pop on change, big values short ("12.5K"); gains flash green, losses red.
- Every action gives feedback: toast, floating "+N" or reward popup. Max 3 toasts.
- Mobile first: 1280x720 offsets under a viewport UIScale (`Theme.screen`), safe insets, buttons >= 44 px, nothing key in the top-left (Roblox menu).
- HUD hugs the edges, centre stays clear; windows open over a dim backdrop with a close X.
- World prices on BillboardGuis: green when affordable, red when not.
- UI is built in code with Instance.new, no image asset ids (emoji/letters for icons), ResetOnSpawn = false.

### Theme.luau (Always first in a UI file: palette, fonts, corner/stroke/gradient/shadow/tween/pop/punch helpers, Theme.screen() for a ScreenGui that scales on phones.)
```luau
-- Theme: palette, fonts and style helpers every other UI kit snippet uses. Paste it first, once per LocalScript.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local Theme = {
	Ink = Color3.fromRGB(28, 22, 38), Cream = Color3.fromRGB(255, 248, 232),
	Primary = Color3.fromRGB(255, 196, 41), Good = Color3.fromRGB(88, 214, 92),
	Bad = Color3.fromRGB(240, 68, 64), Info = Color3.fromRGB(64, 170, 255), Gem = Color3.fromRGB(190, 92, 255),
	Header = Enum.Font.LuckiestGuy, Body = Enum.Font.FredokaOne, Stroke = 3, Radius = 12,
}

function Theme.corner(gui: GuiObject, r: number?)
	local c = Instance.new("UICorner")
	c.CornerRadius = UDim.new(0, r or Theme.Radius)
	c.Parent = gui
end

-- border=true outlines the box; default outlines the text glyphs (the chunky game look).
function Theme.stroke(gui: GuiObject, px: number?, color: Color3?, border: boolean?): UIStroke
	local s = Instance.new("UIStroke")
	s.Thickness = px or Theme.Stroke
	s.Color = color or Theme.Ink
	s.ApplyStrokeMode = if border then Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Border else Enum.ApplyStrokeMode.Contextual
	s.Parent = gui
	return s
end

function Theme.gradient(gui: GuiObject, base: Color3)
	local g = Instance.new("UIGradient")
	g.Rotation = 90
	g.Color = ColorSequence.new(base:Lerp(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), 0.35), base:Lerp(Color3.new(), 0.12))
	g.Parent = gui
end

-- Hard drop shadow behind gui (same parent, ZIndex - 1). Call after gui is parented.
function Theme.shadow(gui: GuiObject, px: number?): Frame
	local sh = Instance.new("Frame")
	sh.AnchorPoint, sh.Size = gui.AnchorPoint, gui.Size
	sh.Position = gui.Position + UDim2.fromOffset(0, px or 5)
	sh.BackgroundColor3, sh.BackgroundTransparency, sh.BorderSizePixel = Theme.Ink, 0.4, 0
	sh.ZIndex = gui.ZIndex - 1
	Theme.corner(sh)
	sh.Parent = gui.Parent
	return sh
end

function Theme.tween(inst: Instance, t: number, props: { [string]: any }, style: Enum.EasingStyle?): Tween
	local tw = TweenService:Create(inst, TweenInfo.new(t, style or Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), props)
	tw:Play()
	return tw
end

local function juiceScale(gui: GuiObject): UIScale
	local s = gui:FindFirstChild("Juice") or Instance.new("UIScale")
	s.Name, s.Parent = "Juice", gui
	return s :: UIScale
end

function Theme.pop(gui: GuiObject, t: number?) -- appear: scale 0 -> 1 with Back overshoot
	local s = juiceScale(gui)
	s.Scale = 0
	Theme.tween(s, t or 0.3, { Scale = 1 }, Enum.EasingStyle.Back)
end

function Theme.punch(gui: GuiObject, amount: number?) -- react: 1.2 -> 1
	local s = juiceScale(gui)
	s.Scale = 1 + (amount or 0.2)
	Theme.tween(s, 0.25, { Scale = 1 }, Enum.EasingStyle.Back)
end

-- Design in 1280x720 offsets; the UIScale fits it to any screen, safe insets keep it off notches.
function Theme.screen(name: string, order: number?): ScreenGui
	local gui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
	gui.Name, gui.ResetOnSpawn, gui.DisplayOrder = name, false, order or 0
	gui.ZIndexBehavior, gui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling, Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets
	local scale = Instance.new("UIScale")
	local cam = workspace.CurrentCamera or workspace:WaitForChild("Camera")
	local function fit()
		local v = cam.ViewportSize
		scale.Scale = math.clamp(math.min(v.X / 1280, v.Y / 720), 0.6, 1.4)
	end
	fit()
	cam:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(fit)
	scale.Parent = gui
	gui.Parent = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
	return gui
end
```

### ChunkyText.luau (Any TextLabel players must read: titles, labels, timers, status text.)
```luau
-- ChunkyText: big outlined game text (titles, numbers, labels). Use for any TextLabel players must read.
local function chunkyText(parent: Instance, text: string, size: UDim2, pos: UDim2, color: Color3?, header: boolean?): TextLabel
	local l = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	l.Text, l.Size, l.Position = text, size, pos
	l.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	l.Font = if header then Theme.Header else Theme.Body
	l.TextColor3 = color or Theme.Cream
	l.TextScaled = true
	local cap = Instance.new("UITextSizeConstraint") -- TextScaled fills the box; cap it so it stays even
	cap.MinTextSize, cap.MaxTextSize = 14, 72
	cap.Parent = l
	Theme.stroke(l, if header then 4 else 3) -- the thick dark outline is what makes text read as "game"
	l.ZIndex = 3
	l.Parent = parent
	return l
end
```

```luau
--!nonstrict
-- ShopUi.client: client-only shop panel (SHOP button + upgrade cards). Sends intent only.
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local UiTheme = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("UiTheme"))
local Upgrades = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Upgrades"))

local buyRemote = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("BuyUpgrade", 10)
local syncRemote = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ShopSync", 10)
if not buyRemote or not syncRemote then
	warn("[ShopUi] shop remotes missing; shop disabled")
	return
end

local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

local ownedSet = {}
local cash = 0
local cards = {}
local lastBuy = 0

-- Effect text built from the exact effect fields in Upgrades
local function effectText(u)
	local e = u.effect
	if type(e) ~= "table" then
		return ""
	end
	if e.kind == "dropper" then
		return "Droppers: " .. tostring(e.slots)
	elseif e.kind == "tier" then
		local ore = Upgrades.ores[e.tier]
		if ore then
			return ore.name .. " ore, $" .. tostring(ore.value) .. " each"
		end
		return "Ore tier " .. tostring(e.tier)
	elseif e.kind == "speed" then
		return "Conveyor speed x" .. tostring(e.mult)
	elseif e.kind == "cashMult" then
		return "Cash payout x" .. tostring(e.mult)
	end
	return tostring(e.kind)
end

local function swatchColor(u)
	local e = u.effect
	if type(e) == "table" then
		if e.kind == "tier" and Upgrades.ores[e.tier] then
			return Upgrades.ores[e.tier].color
		elseif e.kind == "dropper" then
			return UiTheme.info
		elseif e.kind == "speed" then
			return UiTheme.good
		end
	end
	return UiTheme.accent
end

gui.ResetOnSpawn = false

gui.ZIndexBehavior = Enum.ZIndexBehavior.Sibling

local panel = Instance.new("Frame")
panel.Name = "Panel"
panel.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
panel.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.54, 0.5)
panel.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.82, 0.8)
panel.BackgroundColor3 = UiTheme.panel
panel.BorderSizePixel = 0
panel.Visible = false
panel.ZIndex = 1
panel.Parent = gui
UiTheme.roundify(panel, 18)

local function refresh()
	for _, c in ipairs(cards) do
		local u = c.upgrade
		local owned = ownedSet[u.id] == true
		local reqName = nil
		if u.requires and not ownedSet[u.requires] then
			local req = Upgrades.byId[u.requires]
			reqName = req and req.name or tostring(u.requires)
		end
		local dimmed = (not owned) and cash < u.cost
		c.frame.BackgroundTransparency = dimmed and 0.45 or 0
		c.name.TextColor3 = dimmed and UiTheme.locked or UiTheme.text
		c.effect.TextColor3 = dimmed and UiTheme.locked or UiTheme.text
		c.cost.TextColor3 = dimmed and UiTheme.locked or UiTheme.text
		c.swatch.BackgroundTransparency = dimmed and 0.5 or 0
		c.cost.Text = "$" .. tostring(u.cost)
		local b = c.button
		if owned then
			b.Text = "Owned"
			b.BackgroundColor3 = UiTheme.dim
			b.AutoButtonColor = false
			b.Active = false
		elseif reqName then
			b.Text = "Locked (needs " .. reqName .. ")"
			b.BackgroundColor3 = UiTheme.locked
			b.AutoButtonColor = false
			b.Active = false
		else
			b.Text = "Buy"
			b.BackgroundColor3 = dimmed and UiTheme.dim or UiTheme.good
			b.AutoButtonColor = true
			b.Active = true
		end
		b.TextWrapped = true
	end
end

local function tryBuy(card)
	local u = card.upgrade
	if ownedSet[u.id] then
		return
	end
	if u.requires and not ownedSet[u.requires] then
		return
	end
	if os.clock() - lastBuy < 0.4 then
		return
	end
	if cash < u.cost then
		local b = card.button
		b.BackgroundColor3 = UiTheme.bad
		task.delay(0.25, refresh)
		return
	end
	lastBuy = os.clock()
	buyRemote:FireServer(u.id)
end

-- Open/close
local isOpen = false
local function setOpen(open)
	if open == isOpen then
		return
	end
	isOpen = open
	if open then
		panel.Visible = true
		panelScale.Scale = 0
		TweenService:Create(panelScale, TweenInfo.new(0.3, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), { Scale = 1 }):Play()
		syncRemote:FireServer()
		refresh()
	else
		local tw = TweenService:Create(panelScale, TweenInfo.new(0.15, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In), { Scale = 0 })
		tw.Completed:Connect(function()
			if not isOpen then
				panel.Visible = false
			end
		end)
		tw:Play()
	end
end
```
